Description:
This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query. The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

Description:
This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

1. File Retrieval Engine Architecture
   The File Retrieval Engine must adhere to the architecture shown in Figure 1 and must contain and implement the following three components: AppInterface, ProcessingEngine and IndexStore.
   The IndexStore component is responsible with storing the DocumentMap and the TermInvertedIndex indexes, and it exposes four services: putDocument, getDocument, updated Index and lookupIndex.
   The DocumentMap index stores a mapping between the relative path of documents and a unique document number. The document number can be generated incrementally as documents get indexed by the FileRetrievalEngine, and this technique is used to minimize the amount of memory used by the TermInvertedIndex.

The indexFolder method receives as an argument an input folder path and builds an index from all the documents found in the folder. It firstly needs to crawl the folder, create a list of document paths, and call putDocument to receive a document number for each document. Then, it must extract all words that contain alphanumeric, underscore, and hyphen characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-] that have a length greater than 3. Any character that is not alphanumeric, an underscore, or a hyphen is considered a delimiter. While extracting the words/terms, the program must count the number of occurrences/frequency of each unique word/term in the document. For each document, after it extracted all the unique words and after it computed the frequencies, the ProcessingEngine will then update the IndexStore by calling updateIndex.

The ProcessingEngine component is responsible for indexing the documents read from an input folder and for processing search commands. The ProcessingEngine will use the services provided by the IndexStore to store and access the document mapping and the term inverted index. The ProcessingEngine exposes two services: indexFolder and search.

The indexFolder method receives as an argument an input folder path and builds an index from all the documents found in the folder. It firstly needs to crawl the folder, create a list of document paths, and call putDocument to receive a document number for each document. Then, it must extract all words that contain alphanumeric, underscore, and hyphen characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-] that have a length greater than 3. Any character that is not alphanumeric, an underscore, or a hyphen is considered a delimiter. While extracting the words/terms, the program must count the number of occurrences/frequency of each unique word/term in the document. For each document, after it extracted all the unique words and after it computed the frequencies, the ProcessingEngine will then update the IndexStore by calling updateIndex.

The search method receives as an argument a list of terms from an AND query and returns as a result the list of documents that contain all the terms and the combined number of occurrences per document for all terms. Your program needs to support queries that can have up to 3 terms. To calculate the result for a search query,

For each document, after it extracted all the unique words and after it computed the frequencies, the ProcessingEngine will then update the IndexStore by calling updateIndex.

The search method receives as an argument a list of terms from an AND query and returns as a result the list of documents that contain all the terms and the combined number of occurrences per document for all terms. Your program needs to support queries that can have up to 3 terms. To calculate the result for a search query, the ProcessingEngine needs to call for each input term lookupIndex. Then it must combine the results for each term by implementing an intersection mechanism

This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

will use the services provided by the IndexStore to store and access the document mapping and the term inverted index. The ProcessingEngine exposes two services: indexFolder and search.

The indexFolder method receives as an argument an input folder path and builds an index from all the documents found in the folder. It firstly needs to crawl the folder, create a list of document paths, and call putDocument to receive a document number for each document. Then, it must extract all words that contain alphanumeric, underscore, and hyphen characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-] that have a length greater than 3. Any character that is not alphanumeric, an underscore, or a hyphen is considered a delimiter. While extracting the words/terms, the program must count the number of occurrences/frequency of each unique word/term in the document. For each document, after it extracted all the unique words and after it computed the frequencies, the ProcessingEngine will then update the IndexStore by calling updateIndex.

The search method receives as an argument a list of terms from an AND query and returns as a result the list of documents that contain all the terms and the combined number of occurrences per document for all terms. Your program needs to support queries that can have up to 3 terms. To calculate the result for a search query, the ProcessingEngine needs to call for each input term lookupIndex. Then it must combine the results for each term by implementing an intersection mechanism

alphanumeric, underscore, and hyphen characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-] that have a length greater than 3. Any character that is not alphanumeric, an underscore, or a hyphen is considered a delimiter. While extracting the words/terms, the program must count the number of occurrences/frequency of each unique word/term in the document. The search method receives as an argument a list of terms from an AND query and returns as a result the list of documents that contain all the terms and the combined number of occurrences per document for all terms. Your program needs to support queries that can have up to 3 terms. To calculate the result for a search query, the ProcessingEngine needs to call for each input term lookupIndex. Then it must combine the results for each term by implementing an intersection mechanism that has the following rules: if a document number exists in all lookup results, include it in the final result, and the frequency of the final result will be calculated as the sum of frequencies between all results for each document number. Then, the ProcessingEngine must call getDocument to get the document paths and must sort the final list of pairs of document paths and frequencies firstly in descending order by frequency and secondly in ascending lexicographic order by document path. This means that documents that have similar frequencies must be sorted in lexicographic order by document path.

2. File Retrieval Engine CLI Specification

The File Retrieval Engine must support the following commands:

- quit: this command closes the application by gracefully.

- index <folder path>: this command needs to tell the File Retrieval Engine to crawl and find all the documents in the given folder path, and must build an index from those documents. Sequences of alphanumeric, underscore and hyphen characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-] that are separated by any other character(s) and are larger than 3 characters are considered as terms that need to be indexed.

- search <AND query>: this command needs to tell the File Retrieval Engine to process a search query. The search query is expressed as an AND query, that returns all the documents that contain all the terms from the AND query. The returned documents are to be sorted by the number of accumulated occurrences of all terms in each document and in lexicographic order of document path, and only the top 10 documents need to be printed to screen. For example, if the user inputs the following query: cats AND dogs, the File Retrieval Engine must return all documents that contain cats and dogs, must sort the returned documents by the total number of occurrences of both cats and dogs in each document and in lexicographic order of document path, and must return only the top 10 documents.

Text:
The File Retrieval Engine must support the following commands:

- quit: this command closes the application by gracefully.

- index <folder path>: this command needs to tell the File Retrieval Engine to crawl and find all the documents in the given folder path, and must build an index from those documents. Sequences of alphanumeric, underscore and hyphen characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-] that are separated by any other character(s) and are larger than 3 characters are considered as terms that need to be indexed.

- search <AND query>: this command needs to tell the File Retrieval Engine to process a search query. The search query is expressed as an AND query, that returns all the documents that contain all the terms from the AND query. The returned documents are to be sorted by the number of accumulated occurrences of all terms in each document and in lexicographic order of document path, and only the top 10 documents need to be printed to screen. For example, if the user inputs the following query: cats AND dogs, the File Retrieval Engine must return all documents that contain cats and dogs, must sort the returned documents by the total number of occurrences of both cats and dogs in each document and in lexicographic order of document path, and must return only the top 10 documents.

- quit: this command closes the application by gracefully.

- index <folder path>: this command needs to tell the File Retrieval Engine to crawl and find all the documents in the given folder path, and must build an index from those documents. Sequences of alphanumeric, underscore and hyphen characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-] that are separated by any other character(s) and are larger than 3 characters are considered as terms that need to be indexed.

- search <AND query>: this command needs to tell the File Retrieval Engine to process a search query. The search query is expressed as an AND query, that returns all the documents that contain all the terms from the AND query. The returned documents are to be sorted by the number of accumulated occurrences of all terms in each document and in lexicographic order of document path, and only the top 10 documents need to be printed to screen. For example, if the user inputs the following query: cats AND dogs, the File Retrieval Engine must return all documents that contain cats and dogs, must sort the returned documents by the total number of occurrences of both cats and dogs in each document and in lexicographic order of document path, and must return only the top 10 documents.

For example, if the user inputs the following query: cats AND dogs, the File Retrieval Engine must return all documents that contain cats and dogs, must sort the returned documents by the total number of occurrences of both cats and dogs in each document and in lexicographic order of document path, and must return only the top 10 documents.

Top: 2. File Retrieval Engine CLI Specification

Text:
The File Retrieval Engine must support the following commands:

- quit: this command closes the application by gracefully.

- index <folder path>: this command needs to tell the File Retrieval Engine to crawl and find all the documents in the given folder path, and must build an index from those documents. Sequences of alphanumeric, underscore and hyphen characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-] that are separated by any other character(s) and are larger than 3 characters are considered as terms that need to be indexed.

- search <AND query>: this command needs to tell the File Retrieval Engine to process a search query. The search query is expressed as an AND query, that returns all the documents that contain all the terms from the AND query. The returned documents are to be sorted by the number of accumulated occurrences of all terms in each document and in lexicographic order of document path, and only the top 10 documents need to be printed to screen. For example, if the user inputs the following query: cats AND dogs, the File Retrieval Engine must return all documents that contain cats and dogs, must sort the returned documents by the total number of occurrences of both cats and dogs in each document and in lexicographic order of document path, and must return only the top 10 documents.

The ProcessingEngine component is responsible for indexing the documents read from an input folder and for processing search commands. The ProcessingEngine will use the services provided by the IndexStore to store and access the document mapping and the term inverted index. The ProcessingEngine exposes two services: indexFolder and search.

The indexFolder method receives as an argument an input folder path and builds an index from all the documents found in the folder. It firstly needs to crawl the folder, create a list of document paths, and call putDocument to receive a document number for each document. Then, it must extract all words that contain alphanumeric, underscore, and hyphen characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-] that have a length greater than 3. Any character that is not alphanumeric, an underscore, or a hyphen is considered a delimiter. While extracting the words/terms, the program must count the number of occurrences/frequency of each unique word/term in the document. For each document, after it extracted all the unique words and after it computed the frequencies, the ProcessingEngine will then update the IndexStore by calling updateIndex.

The search method receives as an argument a list of terms from an AND query and returns as a result the list of documents that contain all the terms and the combined number of occurrences per document for all terms. Your program needs to support queries that can have up to 3 terms. To calculate the result for a search query,

will use the services provided by the IndexStore to store and access the document mapping and the term inverted index. The ProcessingEngine exposes two services: indexFolder and search.

The indexFolder method receives as an argument an input folder path and builds an index from all the documents found in the folder. It firstly needs to crawl the folder, create a list of document paths, and call putDocument to receive a document number for each document. Then, it must extract all words that contain alphanumeric, underscore, and hyphen characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-] that have a length greater than 3. Any character that is not alphanumeric, an underscore, or a hyphen is considered a delimiter. While extracting the words/terms, the program must count the number of occurrences/frequency of each unique word/term in the document. For each document, after it extracted all the unique words and after it computed the frequencies, the ProcessingEngine will then update the IndexStore by calling updateIndex.

The search method receives as an argument a list of terms from an AND query and returns as a result the list of documents that contain all the terms and the combined number of occurrences per document for all terms. Your program needs to support queries that can have up to 3 terms. To calculate the result for a search query, the ProcessingEngine needs to call for each input term lookupIndex. Then it must combine the results for each term by implementing an intersection mechanism

The search method receives as an argument a list of terms from an AND query and returns as a result the list of documents that contain all the terms and the combined number of occurrences per document for all terms. Your program needs to support queries that can have up to 3 terms. To calculate the result for a search query, the ProcessingEngine needs to call for each input term lookupIndex. Then it must combine the results for each term by implementing an intersection mechanism

   The File Retrieval Engine must adhere to the architecture shown in Figure 1 and must contain and implement the following three components: AppInterface, ProcessingEngine and IndexStore.

   The File Retrieval Engine must adhere to the architecture shown in Figure 1 and must contain and implement the following three components: AppInterface, ProcessingEngine and IndexStore.

   The File Retrieval Engine must adhere to the architecture shown in Figure 1 and must contain and implement the following three components: AppInterface, ProcessingEngine and IndexStore.

   The File Retrieval Engine must adhere to the architecture shown in Figure 1 and must contain and implement the following three components: AppInterface, ProcessingEngine and IndexStore.

   The File Retrieval Engine must adhere to the architecture shown in Figure 1 and must contain and implement the following three components: AppInterface, ProcessingEngine and IndexStore.

   The File Retrieval Engine must adhere to the architecture shown in Figure 1 and must contain and implement the following three components: AppInterface, ProcessingEngine and IndexStore.

   The File Retrieval Engine must adhere to the architecture shown in Figure 1 and must contain and implement the following three components: AppInterface, ProcessingEngine and IndexStore.
   The IndexStore component is responsible with storing the DocumentMap and the TermInvertedIndex indexes, and it exposes four services: putDocument, getDocument, updated Index and lookupIndex.

   The File Retrieval Engine must adhere to the architecture shown in Figure 1 and must contain and implement the following three components: AppInterface, ProcessingEngine and IndexStore.
   The IndexStore component is responsible with storing the DocumentMap and the TermInvertedIndex indexes, and it exposes four services: putDocument, getDocument, updated Index and lookupIndex.

The document number can be generated incrementally as documents get indexed by the FileRetrievalEngine, and this technique is used to minimize the amount of memory used by the TermInvertedIndex.

   The File Retrieval Engine must adhere to the architecture shown in Figure 1 and must contain and implement the following three components: AppInterface, ProcessingEngine and IndexStore.
   The IndexStore component is responsible with storing the DocumentMap and the TermInvertedIndex indexes, and it exposes four services: putDocument, getDocument, updated Index and lookupIndex.

   The File Retrieval Engine must adhere to the architecture shown in Figure 1 and must contain and implement the following three components: AppInterface, ProcessingEngine and IndexStore.

   The File Retrieval Engine must adhere to the architecture shown in Figure 1 and must contain and implement the following three components: AppInterface, ProcessingEngine and IndexStore.

   The File Retrieval Engine must adhere to the architecture shown in Figure 1 and must contain and implement the following three components: AppInterface, ProcessingEngine and IndexStore.

   The File Retrieval Engine must adhere to the architecture shown in Figure 1 and must contain and implement the following three components: AppInterface, ProcessingEngine and IndexStore.
   The IndexStore component is responsible with storing the DocumentMap and the TermInvertedIndex indexes, and it exposes four services: putDocument, getDocument, updated Index and lookupIndex.
   The DocumentMap index stores a mapping between the relative path of documents and a unique document number. The document number can be generated incrementally as documents get indexed by the FileRetrievalEngine, and this technique is used to minimize the amount of memory used by the TermInvertedIndex.

This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

will use the services provided by the IndexStore to store and access the document mapping and the term inverted index. The ProcessingEngine exposes two services: indexFolder and search.

The indexFolder method receives as an argument an input folder path and builds an index from all the documents found in the folder. It firstly needs to crawl the folder, create a list of document paths, and call putDocument to receive a document number for each document. Then, it must extract all words that contain alphanumeric, underscore, and hyphen characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-] that have a length greater than 3. Any character that is not alphanumeric, an underscore, or a hyphen is considered a delimiter. While extracting the words/terms, the program must count the number of occurrences/frequency of each unique word/term in the document. For each document, after it extracted all the unique words and after it computed the frequencies, the ProcessingEngine will then update the IndexStore by calling updateIndex.

The search method receives as an argument a list of terms from an AND query and returns as a result the list of documents that contain all the terms and the combined number of occurrences per document for all terms. Your program needs to support queries that can have up to 3 terms. To calculate the result for a search query, the ProcessingEngine needs to call for each input term lookupIndex. Then it must combine the results for each term by implementing an intersection mechanism

will use the services provided by the IndexStore to store and access the document mapping and the term inverted index. The ProcessingEngine exposes two services: indexFolder and search.

It firstly needs to crawl the folder, create a list of document paths, and call putDocument to receive a document number for each document. Then, it must extract all words that contain alphanumeric, underscore, and hyphen characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-] that have a length greater than 3. Any character that is not alphanumeric, an underscore, or a hyphen is considered a delimiter. While extracting the words/terms, the program must count the number of occurrences/frequency of each unique word/term in the document. For each document, after it extracted all the unique words and after it computed the frequencies, the ProcessingEngine will then update the IndexStore by calling updateIndex.

The search method receives as an argument a list of terms from an AND query and returns as a result the list of documents that contain all the terms and the combined number of occurrences per document for all terms. Your program needs to support queries that can have up to 3 terms. To calculate the result for a search query, the ProcessingEngine needs to call for each input term lookupIndex. Then it must combine the results for each term by implementing an intersection mechanism

Then, it must extract all words that contain alphanumeric, underscore, and hyphen characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-] that have a length greater than 3. Any character that is not alphanumeric, an underscore, or a hyphen is considered a delimiter. While extracting the words/terms, the program must count the number of occurrences/frequency of each unique word/term in the document. For each document, after it extracted all the unique words and after it computed the frequencies, the ProcessingEngine will then update the IndexStore by calling updateIndex.

The search method receives as an argument a list of terms from an AND query and returns as a result the list of documents that contain all the terms and the combined number of occurrences per document for all terms. Your program needs to support queries that can have up to 3 terms. To calculate the result for a search query, the ProcessingEngine needs to call for each input term lookupIndex. Then it must combine the results for each term by implementing an intersection mechanism

Maximum points: 100
- This programming assignment must be done individually.

This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

时间戳: 00:55:02 (3302.00s), OCR耗时: 0.00s, 平均耗时: 1.60s, InputTokens: 0, OutputTokens: 0
============================================================
Type: document

Content: 
alphanumeric, underscore, and hyphen characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-] that have a length greater than 3. Any character that is not alphanumeric, an underscore, or a hyphen is considered a delimiter. While extracting the words/terms, the program must count the number of occurrences/frequency of each unique word/term in the document. For each document, after it extracted all the unique words and after it computed the frequencies, the ProcessingEngine will then update the IndexStore by calling updateIndex.

The search method receives as an argument a list of terms from an AND query and returns as a result the list of documents that contain all the terms and the combined number of occurrences per document for all terms. Your program needs to support queries that can have up to 3 terms. To calculate the result for a search query, the ProcessingEngine needs to call for each input term lookupIndex. Then it must combine the results for each term by implementing an intersection mechanism that has the following rules: if a document number exists in all lookup results, include it in the final result, and the frequency of the final result will be calculated as the sum of frequencies between all results for each document number. Then, the ProcessingEngine must call getDocument to get the document paths and must sort the final list of pairs of document paths and frequencies firstly in descending order by frequency and secondly in ascending lexicographic order by document path. This means that documents that have similar frequencies must be sorted in lexicographic order by document path.

Content:
Top: The DocumentMap index stores a mapping between the relative path of documents and a unique document number. The document number can be generated incrementally as documents get indexed by the FileRetrievalEngine, and this technique is used to minimize the amount of memory used by the TermInvertedIndex. The DocumentMap can be updated through the putDocument method, that receives as an input a document path and returns a unique document number, and it can be read through the getDocument document method, twichreceives a document number as the input and returns the document path.

Middle: The TermInvertedIndex index stores a dictionary where the keys are words/terms extracted from the documents and the values are a list of pairs of two numbers. The first number in each pair is the document number, and the second number is the number of times the word/term appeared in the document. The TermInvertedIndex

Code: package csc435.app;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.HashMap;

// Data structure that stores a document number and the number of time a word/term appears in
class DocFreqPair {
    public long documentNumber;
    public long wordFrequency;

    public DocFreqPair(long documentNumber, long wordFrequency) {
        this.documentNumber = documentNumber;
        this.wordFrequency = wordFrequency;
    }
}

class DocPathFreqPair {

    public long wordFrequency;

    public DocPathFreqPair(String documentPath, long wordFrequency) {
        this.documentPath = documentPath;
        this.wordFrequency = wordFrequency;
    }

    public double executionTime;
    public ArrayList<DocPathFreqPair> documentFrequencies;

    public SearchResult(double executionTime, ArrayList<DocPathFreqPair> documentFrequencies) {
        this.executionTime = executionTime;
        this.documentFrequencies = documentFrequencies;

}

class DocPathFreqPair {
    public String documentPath;
    public long wordFrequency;

    public DocPathFreqPair(String documentPath, long wordFrequency) {
        this.documentPath = documentPath;
        this.wordFrequency = wordFrequency;
    }
}

class SearchResult {
    public double executionTime;
    public ArrayList<DocPathFreqPair> documentFrequencies;

    public SearchResult(double executionTime, ArrayList<DocPathFreqPair> documentFrequencies) {
        this.executionTime = executionTime;
        this.documentFrequencies = documentFrequencies;
    }

#include <string>

AppInterface::AppInterface(std::shared_ptr<ProcessingEngine> engine) : engine(engine) { }

void AppInterface::readCommands() {
    // TO-DO implement the read commands method
    std::string command;

    while (true) {
        std::cout << "> ";
        // read from command line
        std::getline(std::cin, command);

        // if the command is quit, terminate the program
        if (command == "quit") {
            break;
        }

        // if the command begins with index, index the files from the specified directory
        if (command.size() >= 5 && command.substr(0, 5) == "index") {
            // TO-DO parse command and call indexFolder on the processing engine

AppInterface::AppInterface(std::shared_ptr<ProcessingEngine> engine) : engine(engine) { }

void AppInterface::readCommands() {
    // TO-DO implement the read commands method
    std::string command;

    while (true) {
        std::cout << "> ";
        // read from command line
        std::getline(std::cin, command);

        // if the command is quit, terminate the program
        if (command == "quit") {
            break;
        }

        // if the command begins with index, index the files from the specified directory
        if (command.size() >= 5 && command.substr(0, 5) == "index") {
            // TO-DO parse command and call indexFolder on the processing engine
            // TO-DO print the execution time and the total number of bytes read
            continue;
        }
    }
}

#include <string>

AppInterface::AppInterface(std::shared_ptr<ProcessingEngine> engine) : engine(engine) { }

void AppInterface::readCommands() {
    // TO-DO implement the read commands method
    std::string command;

    while (true) {
        std::cout << "> ";
        // read from command line
        std::getline(std::cin, command);

        // if the command is quit, terminate the program
        if (command == "quit") {
            break;
        }

        // if the command begins with index, index the files from the specified directory
        if (command.size() >= 5 && command.substr(0, 5) == "index") {
            // TO-DO parse command and call indexFolder on the processing engine
            // TO-DO print the execution time and the total number of bytes read
            continue;
        }
    }
}

type IndexResult struct {
	ExecutionTime float64
	TotalBytesRead int64

type DocPathFreqPair struct {

    // TO-DO implement the read commands method
    std::string command;

    while (true) {
        std::cout << "> ";
        // read from command line

package main

type IndexResult struct {
	ExecutionTime float64
	TotalBytesRead int64
}

type DocPathFreqPair struct {
	DocumentPath string
	WordFrequency int64
}

type SearchResult struct {
	ExecutionTime float64
	DocumentFrequencies []DocPathFreqPair
}

type ProcessingEngine struct {
	// keep a reference to the index store
	store *IndexStore
}

#include <string>

AppInterface::AppInterface(std::shared_ptr<ProcessingEngine> engine) : engine(engine) { }

void AppInterface::readCommands() {
    // TO-DO implement the read commands method
    std::string command;

    while (true) {
        std::cout << "> ";
        // read from command line
        std::getline(std::cin, command);

        // if the command is quit, terminate the program
        if (command == "quit") {
            break;
        }

        // if the command begins with index, index the files from the specified directory
        if (command.size() >= 5 && command.substr(0, 5) == "index") {
            // TO-DO parse command and call indexFolder on the processing engine
            // TO-DO print the execution time and the total number of bytes read
            continue;
        }
    }
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3.14
import os
import shutil
import subprocess

REPO_URL = "https://neutron.cdm.depaul.edu/csc-435/assignments/csc-435-auto-grader.git"

def main():
    # Clone the auto-grader repository into the test folder
    clone_dir = os.path.join('test', 'auto-grader')
    if os.path.exists(clone_dir):
        print(f"Updating existing repository at {clone_dir}...")
        subprocess.run(["git", "pull"], cwd=clone_dir, check=True)
    else:
        print(f"Cloning {REPO_URL} into {clone_dir}...")
        subprocess.run(["git", "clone", REPO_URL, clone_dir], check=True)

    # Copy test/traces folder recursively from the cloned repo to the current repo
    src_traces_dir = os.path.join(clone_dir, 'test', 'traces')
    dst_traces_dir = os.path.join('test', 'traces')
    if os.path.exists(src_traces_dir):
        if os.path.exists(dst_traces_dir):
            print(f"Overwriting existing {dst_traces_dir}")
        shutil.copytree(src_traces_dir, dst_traces_dir)

#!/usr/bin/env python3.14
import os
import shutil
import subprocess

REPO_URL = "https://neutron.cdm.depaul.edu/csc-435/assignments/csc-435-auto-grader.git"

def main():
    # Clone the auto-grader repository into the test folder
    clone_dir = os.path.join('test', 'auto-grader')
    if os.path.exists(clone_dir):
        print(f"Updating existing repository at {clone_dir}...")
        subprocess.run(["git", "pull"], cwd=clone_dir, check=True)
    else:
        print(f"Cloning {REPO_URL} into {clone_dir}...")
        subprocess.run(["git", "clone", REPO_URL, clone_dir], check=True)

    # Copy test/traces folder recursively from the cloned repo to the current repo
    src_traces_dir = os.path.join(clone_dir, 'test', 'traces')
    dst_traces_dir = os.path.join('test', 'traces')
    if os.path.exists(src_traces_dir):
        if os.path.exists(dst_traces_dir):
            print(f"Overwriting existing {dst_traces_dir}")
        shutil.copytree(src_traces_dir, dst_traces_dir)

#!/usr/bin/env python3.14
import os
import shutil
import subprocess

REPO_URL = "https://neutron.cdm.depaul.edu/csc-435/assignments/csc-435-auto-grader.git"

def main():
    # Clone the auto-grader repository into the test folder
    clone_dir = os.path.join('test', 'auto-grader')
    if os.path.exists(clone_dir):
        print(f"Updating existing repository at {clone_dir}...")
        subprocess.run(["git", "pull"], cwd=clone_dir, check=True)
    else:
        print(f"Cloning {REPO_URL} into {clone_dir}...")
        subprocess.run(["git", "clone", REPO_URL, clone_dir], check=True)

    # Copy test/traces folder recursively from the cloned repo to the current repo
    src_traces_dir = os.path.join(clone_dir, 'test', 'traces')
    dst_traces_dir = os.path.join('test', 'traces')
    if os.path.exists(src_traces_dir):
        if os.path.exists(dst_traces_dir):
            print(f"Overwriting existing {dst_traces_dir}")
        shutil.copytree(src_traces_dir, dst_traces_dir)

Import subprocess

REPO_URL = "https://neutron.cdm.depaul.edu/csc-435/assignments/csc-435-auto-grader.git"

def main():
    # Clone the auto-grader repository into the test folder
    clone_dir = os.path.join('test', 'auto-grader')
    if os.path.exists(clone_dir):
        print(f"Updating existing repository at {clone_dir}...")
        subprocess.run(["git", "pull"], cwd=clone_dir, check=True)
    else:
        print(f"Cloning {REPO_URL} into {clone_dir}...")
        subprocess.run(["git", "clone", REPO_URL, clone_dir], check=True)

    # Copy test/traces folder recursively from the cloned repo to the current repo
    src_traces_dir = os.path.join(clone_dir, 'test', 'traces')
    dst_traces_dir = os.path.join('test', 'traces')
    if os.path.exists(src_traces_dir):
        if os.path.exists(dst_traces_dir):
            shutil.rmtree(dst_traces_dir)
            print(f"Overwriting existing {dst_traces_dir}")
            shutil.copytree(src_traces_dir, dst_traces_dir)
            print(f"Copied {src_traces_dir} to {dst_traces_dir}")
        else:
            print(f"Error: {src_traces_dir} not found.")

Code: setup.py
Import subprocess

REPO_URL = "https://neutron.cdm.depaul.edu/csc-435/assignments/csc-435-auto-grader.git"

def main():
    # Clone the auto-grader repository into the test folder
    clone_dir = os.path.join('test', 'auto-grader')
    if os.path.exists(clone_dir):
        print(f"Updating existing repository at {clone_dir}...")
        subprocess.run(["git", "pull"], cwd=clone_dir, check=True)
    else:
        print(f"Cloning {REPO_URL} into {clone_dir}...")
        subprocess.run(["git", "clone", REPO_URL, clone_dir], check=True)

    # Copy test/traces folder recursively from the cloned repo to the current repo
    src_traces_dir = os.path.join(clone_dir, 'test', 'traces')
    dst_traces_dir = os.path.join('test', 'traces')
    if os.path.exists(src_traces_dir):
        if os.path.exists(dst_traces_dir):
            shutil.rmtree(dst_traces_dir)
            print(f"Overwriting existing {dst_traces_dir}")
            shutil.copytree(src_traces_dir, dst_traces_dir)
            print(f"Copied {src_traces_dir} to {dst_traces_dir}")
        else:
            print(f"Error: {src_traces_dir} not found.")

    dst_test_file = os.path.join('test', 'test_driver.py')

your solution. Before you can evaluate your solution you need to download the datasets. You can download the datasets from the following link:
https://depauledu-my.sharepoint.com/:f:/g/personal/aorhean_depaul_edu/Ej4obLnAKMdFh1HidzdIt1oBHY7lvqXoLdKRg-buoisw?e=SWLALa

After you finished downloading the datasets copy them to the dataset directory (create the directory if it does not exist). Here is an example on how you can copy Dataset1 to the remote machine and how to unzip the dataset:

remote-computer$ mkdir datasets
local-computer$ scp dataset1.zip cc@<remote-ip>:<path-to-repo>/datasets/.
remote-computer$ cd <path-to-repo>/datasets
remote-computer$ unzip dataset1.zip

How to build/compile

To build the Rust solution use the following commands:

cd app-rust
cargo build --release

时间戳: 02:04:11 (7451.00s), OCR耗时: 0.00s, 平均耗时: 1.80s, InputTokens: 0, OutputTokens: 0

Type: document

Content:
Maximum points: 100
- This programming assignment must be done individually.
- Please post your questions on the D2L Programming Assignments topic.
- Only the report must be uploaded to D2L. The code must be uploaded to the GitLab repository created for you for this assignment.
- Late submission will be penalized at 20% per late day.

This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query.

The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

Top: This programming assignment aims to teach you about distributed systems architectures, more precisely about Application Layering. As part of this homework assignment, you will need to implement a simple File Retrieval Engine that follows the Application Layering architecture. The File Retrieval Engine must support indexing files from a specified input folder and searching the indexed documents given a user specified multi-term query. The search operation must return the top 10 most relevant documents that match the user specified query. The programs that you need to implement as part of this assignment are limited to the C++, Java, Go and Rust programming languages, and to the standard libraries. You can use any computer to develop the solution for this assignment, but your program must run on a machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server Edition. You may use your own Linux machine or virtual machine to evaluate the indexing performance of your solution.

- Title: Remote Development
- Publisher: Microsoft
- Downloads: 9,035,221
- Rating: ★★★★☆ (119)
- Description: An extension pack that lets you open any folder in a container, on a remote machine, or in WSL and take advantage of VS Code's full feature set.
- Details:
  - Extension Pack (4)
    - WSL: Open any folder in the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL)...
    - Dev Containers: Open any folder or repository inside a Docker container...
    - Remote - SSH: Open any folder on a remote machine using SSH...
    - Remote - Tunnels: Connect to a remote machine through a Tunnel...
- Visual Studio Code Remote Development Extension Pack
  - Description: The Remote Development extension pack allows you to open any folder in a container, on a remote machine, or in the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) and take advantage of VS Code's full feature set. Since this lets you set up a full-time development environment anywhere, you can:
    - Develop on the same operating system you deploy to or use larger, faster, or more specialized hardware than your local machine.
    - Quickly swap between different, separate development environments and make updates without worrying about impacting your local machine.
    - Help new team members / contributors get productive quickly with easily spun up, consistent development containers.
    - Take advantage of a Linux-based tool-chain right from the comfort of Windows from a full-featured development tool.
  - Note: No source code needs to be on your local machine to gain these benefits since Remote Development runs commands and extensions directly on the remote machine.
  - Includes:
    - Remote - SSH: Work with source code in any location by opening folders on a remote machine/VM using SSH. Supports x86_64, ARMv7 (AArch32), and ARMv8 (AArch64) glibc-based Linux, Windows 10/11/Server (1803+), and macOS 10.14+ (Mojave) SSH hosts.
    - Remote - Tunnels: Work with source code in any location by opening folders on a remote machine/VM using a VS Code Tunnel (rather than SSH).
    - Dev Containers: Work with a separate toolchain or container-based application by opening any folder mounted into or inside a container.

    • Dev Containers: Work with a separate toolchain or container-based application by opening any folder mounted into or inside a container.

  Description: An extension pack that lets you open any folder in a container, on a remote machine, or in WSL and take advantage of VS Code's full feature set.

    Dev Containers: Open any folder or repository inside a Docker container.

  Section: Visual Studio Code Remote Development Extension Pack
  Text:
    The Remote Development extension pack allows you to open any folder in a container, on a remote machine, or in the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) and take advantage of VS Code's full feature set. Since this lets you set up a full-time development environment anywhere, you can:
      • Develop on the same operating system you deploy to or use larger, faster, or more specialized hardware than your local machine.
      • Quickly swap between different, separate development environments and make updates without worrying about impacting your local machine.
      • Help new team members / contributors get productive quickly with easily spun up, consistent development containers.
      • Take advantage of a Linux-based toolchain right from the comfort of Windows from a full-featured development tool.
    No source code needs to be on your local machine to gain these benefits since Remote Development runs commands and extensions directly on the remote machine.
    This Remote Development extension pack includes four extensions:
      • Remote - SSH: Work with source code in any location by opening folders on a remote machine/VM using SSH. Supports x86_64, ARM64 (AArch64), and ARMv7 (AArch32) glibc-based Linux, Windows 10/Server (1803+), and macOS 10.14+ (Mojave) SSH hosts.
      • Remote - Tunnels: Work with source code in any location by opening folders on a remote machine/VM using a VS Code Tunnel (rather than SSH).
      • Dev Containers: Work with a separate toolchain or container-based application by opening any folder mounted into or inside a container.

  - Visual Studio Code Remote Development Extension Pack
    - The Remote Development extension pack allows you to open any folder in a container, on a remote machine, or in the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) and take advantage of VS Code's full feature set. Since this lets you set up a full-time development environment anywhere, you can:
      - Develop on the same operating system you deploy to or use larger, faster, or more specialized hardware than your local machine.
      - Quickly swap between different, separate development environments and make updates without worrying about impacting your local machine.
      - Help new team members / contributors get productive quickly with easily spun up, consistent development containers.
      - Take advantage of a Linux-based toolchain right from the comfort of Windows from a full-featured development tool.
    - No source code needs to be on your local machine to gain these benefits since Remote Development runs commands and extensions directly on the remote machine.
    - This Remote Development extension pack includes four extensions:
      - Remote - SSH: Work with source code in any location by opening folders on a remote machine/VM using SSH. Supports x86_64, ARMv7l (AArch64) glibc-based Linux, Windows 10/Server (1803+), and macOS 10.14+ (Mojave) SSH hosts.
      - Remote - Tunnels: Work with source code in any location by opening folders on a remote machine/VM using a VS Code Tunnel (rather than SSH).
      - Dev Containers: Work with a separate toolchain or container-based application by opening any folder mounted into or inside a container.

Type: desktop, application

Content:
Left:
- Remote Explorer
  - Remotes (Tunnels/SSH)
    - Tunnels
      - Sign in to tunnels registered with Microsoft
      - Sign in to tunnels registered with GitHub
    - SSH
      - List of SSH hosts (e.g., gitlab.com, github.com, telos.cdm.depaul.edu, etc.)
      - grid24 section with paths like /home/ubuntu/Workspace/Projects/research/learning-loop-emr, /home/ubuntu/Workspace/Projects/teaching/csc-397-595-lab1, etc.

Right:
- Extension: Remote Development
  - Title: Remote Development
  - Publisher: Microsoft (microsoft.com)
  - Rating: 9,035,221 downloads, 4.5 stars (119 reviews)
  - Description: An extension pack that lets you open any folder in a container, on a remote machine, or in WSL and take advantage of VS Code's full feature set.
  - Actions: Disable, Uninstall, Auto Update
  - Extension Pack (4):
    - WSL: Open any folder in the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) — 162ms
    - Dev Containers: Open any folder or repository inside a Docker container — 42ms
    - Remote - SSH: Open any folder on a remote machine using SSH — 132ms
    - Remote - Tunnels: Connect to a remote machine through a Tunnel — 73ms
  - Visual Studio Code Remote Development Extension Pack
    - Description: Allows opening any folder in a container, on a remote machine, or in WSL and taking advantage of VS Code's full feature set.
    - Bullet points:
      - Develop on the same operating system you deploy to or use larger, faster, or more specialized hardware than your local machine.
      - Quickly swap between different, separate development environments and make updates without worrying about impacting your local machine.
      - Help new team members/contributors get productive quickly with easily spun-up, consistent development containers.
      - Take advantage of a Linux-based toolchain right from the comfort of Windows from a full-featured development tool.
    - Note: No source code needs to be on your local machine to gain these benefits since Remote Development runs commands and extensions directly on the remote machine.
    - Includes four extensions:
      - Remote - SSH: Work with source code in any location by opening folders on a remote machine/VM using SSH. Supports x86_64, ARMv7l (AArch64), and ARM64 (AArch64) glibc-based Linux, Windows 10/Server (1903+), and macOS 10.14+ (Mojave) SSH hosts.
      - Remote - Tunnels: Work with source code in any location by opening folders on a remote machine/VM using a VS Code Tunnel (rather than SSH).
      - Dev Containers: Work with a separate toolchain or container-based application by opening any folder mounted into or inside a container.

    - Description: Allows opening any folder in a container, on a remote machine, or in WSL and taking advantage of VS Code's full feature set.

      - Quickly swap between different, separate development environments and make updates without worrying about impacting your local machine.

      - Take advantage of a Linux-based toolchain right from the comfort of Windows from a full-featured development tool.

      - Remote - Tunnels: Work with source code in any location by opening folders on a remote machine/VM using a VS Code Tunnel (rather than SSH).
      - Dev Containers: Work with a separate toolchain or container-based application by opening any folder mounted into or inside a container.

  - Description: An extension pack that lets you open any folder in a container, on a remote machine, or in WSL and take advantage of VS Code's full feature set.
  - Actions: Disable, Uninstall, Auto Update
  - Extension Pack (4):
    - WSL: Open any folder in the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) — 162ms
    - Dev Containers: Open any folder or repository inside a Docker container — 42ms
    - Remote - SSH: Open any folder on a remote machine using SSH — 132ms
    - Remote - Tunnels: Connect to a remote machine through a Tunnel — 73ms
  - Visual Studio Code Remote Development Extension Pack
    - Description: Allows opening any folder in a container, on a remote machine, or in WSL and taking advantage of VS Code's full feature set.
    - Bullet points:
      - Develop on the same operating system you deploy to or use larger, faster, or more specialized hardware than your local machine.
      - Quickly swap between different, separate development environments and make updates without worrying about impacting your local machine.
      - Help new team members/contributors get productive quickly with easily spun-up, consistent development containers.
      - Take advantage of a Linux-based toolchain right from the comfort of Windows from a full-featured development tool.
    - Note: No source code needs to be on your local machine to gain these benefits since Remote Development runs commands and extensions directly on the remote machine.
    - Includes four extensions:
      - Remote - SSH: Work with source code in any location by opening folders on a remote machine/VM using SSH. Supports x86_64, ARMv7l (AArch64), and ARM64 (AArch64) glibc-based Linux, Windows 10/Server (1903+), and macOS 10.14+ (Mojave) SSH hosts.
      - Remote - Tunnels: Work with source code in any location by opening folders on a remote machine/VM using a VS Code Tunnel (rather than SSH).
      - Dev Containers: Work with a separate toolchain or container-based application by opening any folder mounted into or inside a container.

Right:
- Extension: Remote Development
  - Title: Remote Development
  - Publisher: Microsoft (microsoft.com)
  - Rating: 9,035,221 downloads, 4.5 stars (119 reviews)
  - Description: An extension pack that lets you open any folder in a container, on a remote machine, or in WSL and take advantage of VS Code's full feature set.
  - Actions: Disable, Uninstall, Auto Update
  - Extension Pack (4):
    - WSL: Open any folder in the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) — 162ms
    - Dev Containers: Open any folder or repository inside a Docker container — 42ms
    - Remote - SSH: Open any folder on a remote machine using SSH — 132ms
    - Remote - Tunnels: Connect to a remote machine through a Tunnel — 73ms
  - Visual Studio Code Remote Development Extension Pack
    - Description: Allows opening any folder in a container, on a remote machine, or in WSL and taking advantage of VS Code's full feature set.
    - Bullet points:
      - Develop on the same operating system you deploy to or use larger, faster, or more specialized hardware than your local machine.
      - Quickly swap between different, separate development environments and make updates without worrying about impacting your local machine.
      - Help new team members/contributors get productive quickly with easily spun-up, consistent development containers.
      - Take advantage of a Linux-based toolchain right from the comfort of Windows from a full-featured development tool.
    - Note: No source code needs to be on your local machine to gain these benefits since Remote Development runs commands and extensions directly on the remote machine.
    - Includes four extensions:
      - Remote - SSH: Work with source code in any location by opening folders on a remote machine/VM using SSH. Supports x86_64, ARMv7l (AArch64), and ARM64 (AArch64) glibc-based Linux, Windows 10/Server (1903+), and macOS 10.14+ (Mojave) SSH hosts.
      - Remote - Tunnels: Work with source code in any location by opening folders on a remote machine/VM using a VS Code Tunnel (rather than SSH).
      - Dev Containers: Work with a separate toolchain or container-based application by opening any folder mounted into or inside a container.

Type: slide

Content:
Title: Architectural styles

Section: Basic idea
- A style is formulated in terms of:
  • (replaceable) components with well-defined interfaces
  • the way that components are connected to each other
  • the data exchanged between components
  • how these components and connectors are jointly configured into a system.

Section: Connector
- A mechanism that mediates communication, coordination, or cooperation among components.
- Example: facilities for (remote) procedure call, messaging, or streaming.

Title: Architectural styles

Section: Basic idea
A style is formulated in terms of:
- (replaceable) components with well-defined interfaces
- the way that components are connected to each other
- the data exchanged between components
- how these components and connectors are jointly configured into a system.

Section: Connector
A mechanism that mediates communication, coordination, or cooperation among components.
Example: facilities for (remote) procedure call, messaging, or streaming.

Content:
Top: Application Layering
    Traditional three-layered view
    • Application-interface layer contains units for interfacing to users or external applications
    • Processing layer contains the functions of an application, i.e., without specific data
    • Data layer contains the data that a client wants to manipulate through the application components

Type: slide, diagram

Content:
Top: Object-based style

Essence:
Components are objects, connected to each other through procedure calls.
Objects may be placed on different machines; calls can thus execute across a network.

Left: Diagram showing interconnected objects with arrows labeled "Method call".

Right: Diagram of an object with labeled parts:
- State
- Method (with four boxes)
- Interface

Encapsulation:
Objects are said to encapsulate data and offer methods on that data without revealing the internal implementation.

Essence

============================================================
Type: slide

Content:
Top: Application Layering
    Traditional three-layered view
        • Application-interface layer contains units for interfacing to users or external applications
        • Processing layer contains the functions of an application, i.e., without specific data
        • Data layer contains the data that a client wants to manipulate through the application components
    Observation
        This layering is found in many distributed information systems, using traditional database technology and accompanying applications.

时间戳: 02:27:16 (8836.00s), OCR耗时: 0.00s, 平均耗时: 2.20s, InputTokens: 0, OutputTokens: 0
============================================================
Type: slide

Content:
Title: Architectural styles

Section: Basic idea
A style is formulated in terms of:
- (replaceable) components with well-defined interfaces
- the way that components are connected to each other
- the data exchanged between components
- how these components and connectors are jointly configured into a system.

Section: Connector
A mechanism that mediates communication, coordination, or cooperation among components.
Example: facilities for (remote) procedure call, messaging, or streaming.

Type: slide, diagram

Content:
Title: Layered architecture
Subtitle: Different layered organizations

Diagram (a):
- Label: Request/Response downcall
- Flow: Layer N → Layer N-1 → ... → Layer 2 → Layer 1

Diagram (b):
- Label: One-way call
- Flow: Layer N → Layer N-1 → Layer N-2 → Layer N-3
- Note: Bidirectional arrows between Layer N-1 and Layer N-2

Diagram (c):
- Flow: Layer N → Layer N-1 → Layer N-2
- Arrows: From Layer N-1 to Layer N-2 labeled "Handle"
- Arrow: From Layer N-2 to Layer N-1 labeled "Upcall"

Title: Layered architecture
Subtitle: Different layered organizations

- Label: Request/Response downcall
- Flow: Layer N → Layer N-1 → ... → Layer 2 → Layer 1

- Note: Bidirectional arrows between Layer N-1 and Layer N-2

- Arrows: From Layer N-1 to Layer N-2 labeled "Handle"
- Arrow: From Layer N-2 to Layer N-1 labeled "Upcall"

Type: slide, diagram

Content:
Top: Object-based style
Left: Essence
  Components are objects, connected to each other through procedure calls.
  Objects may be placed on different machines; calls can thus execute across a network.
Diagram (Left): Shows interconnected "Object" boxes with arrows labeled "Method call" between them.
Diagram (Right): Box labeled "Object" with internal parts: "State" (top), "Method" (middle, 4 boxes), "Interface" (bottom).
Bottom: Encapsulation
  Objects are said to encapsulate data and offer methods on that data without revealing the internal implementation.

时间戳: 02:29:46 (8986.00s), OCR耗时: 9.11s, 平均耗时: 2.20s, InputTokens: 1397, OutputTokens: 148
============================================================
Type: slide

Content:
Top: RESTful architectures
Essence
View a distributed system as a collection of resources, individually managed by components. Resources may be added, removed, retrieved, and modified by (remote) applications.
1. Resources are identified through a single naming scheme
2. All services offer the same interface
3. Messages sent to or from a service are fully self-described
4. After executing an operation at a service, that component forgets everything about the caller

Basic operations
Table:
Operation | Description
---|---
PUT | Create a new resource
GET | Retrieve the state of a resource in some representation
DELETE | Delete a resource
POST | Modify a resource by transferring a new state

Bottom: Encapsulation
  Objects are said to encapsulate data and offer methods on that data without revealing the internal implementation.

============================================================
Type: slide

Content:
Top: RESTful architectures
Essence
View a distributed system as a collection of resources, individually managed by components. Resources may be added, removed, retrieved, and modified by (remote) applications.
1. Resources are identified through a single naming scheme
2. All services offer the same interface
3. Messages sent to or from a service are fully self-described
4. After executing an operation at a service, that component forgets everything about the caller

Basic operations
Table:
Operation | Description
---|---
PUT | Create a new resource
GET | Retrieve the state of a resource in some representation
DELETE | Delete a resource
POST | Modify a resource by transferring a new state

Top: Example: Amazon’s Simple Storage Service

Essence

http://BucketName.s3.amazonaws.com/ObjectName

Typical operations

• Create a bucket/object: PUT, along with the URI
• Listing objects: GET on a bucket name
• Reading an object: GET on a full URI

http://BucketName.s3.amazonaws.com/ObjectName

Typical operations

• Create a bucket/object: PUT, along with the URI
• Listing objects: GET on a bucket name
• Reading an object: GET on a full URI

http://BucketName.s3.amazonaws.com/ObjectName

Typical operations
All operations are carried out by sending HTTP requests:
• Create a bucket/object: PUT, along with the URI
• Listing objects: GET on a bucket name
• Reading an object: GET on a full URI

http://BucketName.s3.amazonaws.com/ObjectName

Typical operations
All operations are carried out by sending HTTP requests:
• Create a bucket/object: PUT, along with the URI
• Listing objects: GET on a bucket name
• Reading an object: GET on a full URI

http://BucketName.s3.amazonaws.com/ObjectName

Typical operations

• Create a bucket/object: PUT, along with the URI
• Listing objects: GET on a bucket name
• Reading an object: GET on a full URI

http://BucketName.s3.amazonaws.com/ObjectName

Typical operations

• Create a bucket/object: PUT, along with the URI
• Listing objects: GET on a bucket name
• Reading an object: GET on a full URI

http://BucketName.s3.amazonaws.com/ObjectName

Typical operations

• Create a bucket/object: PUT, along with the URI
• Listing objects: GET on a bucket name
• Reading an object: GET on a full URI
